key_insights: Deferral applies to early action/early decision applicants: the school moves the application into the regular decision pool for re-review instead of an immediate accept/reject
Waitlisting typically happens near the end of the regular decision cycle, for applicants neither accepted nor declined
Being waitlisted means being placed on a list the school may pull from later if spots open after accepted students respond
Some schools never pull anyone from their waitlist, and waitlisted students may never hear back at all
Recommends waitlisted students commit to (deposit at) another accepted school rather than waiting, and only switch if later pulled off the waitlist
notable_or_distinctive: Straightforward, generically accurate explainer distinguishing deferral from waitlisting with practical next-step advice; nothing beyond standard counseling-office framing.
reliability_notes: Short (2 minutes) and general; no data or school-specific figures given to back claims, though the deferral/waitlist mechanics described are standard and uncontroversial.
